title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Evolutionary Biology — 2024
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection with an example.
questions.solution:
**Darwin (1859):** overproduction → variation → struggle for existence → survival of the fittest → inheritance of favourable traits → new species over time.

**Example — industrial melanism:** soot-darkened trees hid dark peppered moths from birds while pale ones were eaten; dark alleles spread until clean-air laws reversed the trend — selection observed in decades.
questions.knowledgeNote: 'Descent with modification' plus genetics became the modern synthesis — Darwin's mechanism, Mendel's inheritance.

questions.question: What are the evidences of evolution? Explain with one example each from morphological and paleontological studies.
questions.solution:
**Morphological:** homologous structures — same bone plan, different jobs (human arm, whale flipper, bat wing prove common ancestry).

**Paleontological:** fossils ordered simple→complex in strata; **Archaeopteryx** bridges reptiles and birds (teeth and claws with feathers).
questions.knowledgeNote: Homologous = shared ancestry; analogous (bird vs insect wings) = convergent function, different origin.

questions.question: Compare Lamarck's and Darwin's theories of evolution.
questions.solution:
**Lamarck:** use and disuse develops organs; acquired characters are inherited (giraffe stretching its neck).

**Darwin:** variation already exists; nature selects the fittest, and only germ-line traits pass on.

Lamarck fails because acquired changes (a blacksmith's muscles) are not inherited — Weismann's mouse-tail experiments disproved it.
questions.knowledgeNote: Lamarck = inheritance of acquired characters; Darwin = selection on variation — one line each settles the comparison.

questions.question: State the Hardy-Weinberg principle. List the factors that disturb genetic equilibrium.
questions.solution:
**Principle:** allele frequencies (p + q = 1; p² + 2pq + q² = 1) stay constant generation after generation in an ideal population.

**Disturbers:** mutation, selection, migration (gene flow), genetic drift (small populations), and non-random mating.
questions.knowledgeNote: The equation is the null hypothesis of evolution — deviation from it MEASURES evolution happening.

questions.question: Distinguish between homologous and analogous organs with one example of each.
questions.solution:
**Homologous:** same origin/structure, different functions — e.g. human forelimb vs bat wing (divergent evolution, common ancestry).

**Analogous:** different origins, same function — e.g. butterfly vs bird wings (convergent evolution, no close ancestry).
questions.knowledgeNote: Vestigial organs (human appendix, whale pelvis) are homology's leftovers — reduced structures proving past function.

questions.question: Outline the stages of human evolution from Dryopithecus to Homo sapiens.
questions.solution: **Dryopithecus** (ape-like, Miocene) → **Ramapithecus** (early hominid) → **Australopithecus** (bipedal, small brain) → **H. habilis** (tool maker) → **H. erectus** (fire, larger brain) → **Neanderthals** (burials) → **H. sapiens** (modern, Cro-Magnon art).
questions.knowledgeNote: Bipedalism came before brain expansion — walking upright freed the hands millions of years before wit followed.
